key_insight: An alternating-minimization control search can synthesize high-fidelity multimode entangling gates in trapped-ion chains by jointly targeting the desired spin-spin couplings and suppressing residual spin-motion entanglement.
engineering_relevance: This makes programmable long-range and local interaction engineering more feasible for large trapped-ion quantum processors using only global laser control or structured individual addressing.
method: Formulate multimode gate design as a high-dimensional non-convex optimization problem over multi-tone control fields.
Use alternating minimization to improve numerical stability while satisfying interaction targets and motional-decoupling constraints.
Demonstrate scalability on large ion chains with all-to-all, nearest-neighbor, and qLDPC-like target interactions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful synthesis for ion chains up to N=1000 with global control and an individual-addressing example at N=512, with control resources not growing rapidly over the explored regimes.
watch_item: The results are based on numerical synthesis and reported parameter regimes, so experimental robustness to noise, calibration error, and hardware constraints still needs validation.
paper_title: Large-scale multimode entangling-gate synthesis in trapped-ion systems
